title_candidates: They Filmed Her When She Hid — Now They Can't Look Away
The Girl Behind the Curtain Was the Story Everyone Wanted
He Knew Her Before the World Called Her Beautiful
logline: In a coastal boarding school where the annual rescue-swim film is shot inside the old tidal pool, Noa, a scholarship pool technician who hides a burn scar and her swimming ability after classmates turned a rescue failure into a humiliating viral clip is pushed toward public transformation, but the love interest is credible only because he witnessed her courage before the world approved of her.
audience_promise: A mobile-native transformation romance in which public gaze inversion, pre-transformation witness, behavioral cost, reciprocal memory debt, and a second performance engine turn visibility into agency rather than mere makeover reward.

emotional_engine.wound: Noa learned that visibility is dangerous because her father taught her to hide the scar and avoid cameras because his own rescue career ended in public blame; public misreading then confirmed the shame.
emotional_engine.want: remain useful and safe without becoming a spectacle again
emotional_engine.need: claim authorship, visibility, and love without treating appearance approval as proof of worth
emotional_engine.injustice: Ilsa, a champion swimmer whose sponsorship depends on staying the school's visible heroine converts status insecurity into public humiliation and image control
emotional_engine.protective_counterforce: Eren, a quiet safety diver who saw Noa keep a younger swimmer alive before the viral clip made her a joke protects the person before the transformation because Eren knows Noa stayed underwater with a panicking child when no camera was recording and trusts that act more than appearance
emotional_engine.belonging_payoff: the pool gallery changes from replay-screen humiliation to a safety community where Noa instructs others openly
emotional_engine.secret_or_power_asymmetry: legacy status, image control, and institutional casting power oppose a scholarship protagonist with no public protection
emotional_engine.cost_of_failure: she retreats into hiding, loses authorship/professional agency, and confirms the false belief that visibility is annihilation

protagonist.identity: Noa, a scholarship pool technician who hides a burn scar and her swimming ability after classmates turned a rescue failure into a humiliating viral clip
protagonist.vulnerability: public shame, image control, family fear, and lack of institutional power
protagonist.capability: craft/professional competence, protective courage, persistence, and the ability to lead others once she stops hiding
protagonist.agency_first_action: she protects or guides a vulnerable person before protecting her image
protagonist.transformation: from protected invisibility to chosen visibility grounded in authorship, competence, consent, and reciprocal recognition

opening_event.first_10_seconds: a future-pressure fragment inside a training documentary about real rescue swimming that turns performance into dangerous physical competence hints that powerful people need the hidden protagonist before the story cuts back to the wound
opening_event.first_60_seconds: Noa is spatially trapped in the tiled pool gallery where students once replayed the humiliating clip and later watch the final drill while others film, laugh, or misread her silence
opening_event.first_5_minutes: the family fear system, the meaning-carrier scratched rescue whistle, and the first pre-transformation protective act are established before the visual transformation
opening_event.dramatic_question: can a protagonist who learned that visibility is dangerous become publicly seen without surrendering authorship or accepting shallow approval?

theme_lane.family_or_heir_hook: protection itself becomes the wound when a family teaches a child to hide in order to survive
theme_lane.romance_hook: Eren, a quiet safety diver who saw Noa keep a younger swimmer alive before the viral clip made her a joke remembers reciprocal courage rather than rewarding beauty
theme_lane.modern_power_hook: viral spectatorship, legacy status, institutional casting, and public image control

transformation_engine.family_protection_wound: her father taught her to hide the scar and avoid cameras because his own rescue career ended in public blame
transformation_engine.pre_transformation_witness: Eren knows Noa stayed underwater with a panicking child when no camera was recording and trusts that act more than appearance
transformation_engine.reciprocal_memory_debt: as children Noa pulled Eren away from a suction grate and told him to breathe before she knew who he was
transformation_engine.behavioral_transformation_cost: breath training, scar exposure, rescue certification, and learning to command a room rather than chasing beauty approval
transformation_engine.second_performance_engine: a training documentary about real rescue swimming that turns performance into dangerous physical competence
transformation_engine.agency_violation: the coach and Eren enter Noa into the documentary without asking after seeing her secret practice footage
transformation_engine.public_space_reversal: the tiled pool gallery where students once replayed the humiliating clip and later watch the final drill
transformation_engine.closure: the pool gallery changes from replay-screen humiliation to a safety community where Noa instructs others openly

nearest_failures: makeover treated as proof of worth
love interest attracted only after transformation
public humiliation without systemic cause or spatial closure
second half repeating jealousy rather than opening a new performance/professional engine
self-destructive despair imagery used as a cheap transformation trigger
mitigations: show transformation as behavior and skill, not only appearance
open a second professional/performance engine after the reveal
make consent violations by allies visible and consequential
counterexamples_checked: beautiful transformation imagery alone does not explain retention
romantic rescue is weak unless reciprocal and pre-transformation
viral attention can repeat the wound rather than repair it

packaging.thumbnail_single_read: Noa centered between public approval and a hostile rival while scratched rescue whistle catches the light
packaging.curiosity_gap: who saw her before the world decided she was worth watching?
packaging.visual_before_after: hidden backstage/pool-floor posture becomes upright public authorship in the same space
packaging.title_thumbnail_mismatch_risk: generic beauty packaging would undersell authorship, consent, and pre-transformation recognition

evidence_boundaries: Inspired by mechanism-level evidence in the EchoDrama Hidden Beauty deep dive; characters, institutions, object, second engine, and ending are original.
No CTR, retention, or traffic causality is claimed from public video metadata.

meaning_carrier.opening_meaning: the whistle belonged to Noa's mother and is treated as a superstitious piece of pool equipment
meaning_carrier.closing_reversal: the same whistle coordinates the final rescue drill and proves Noa's competence without erasing the scar
meaning_carrier.final_sequence_use: the object is used openly in the final authorship/rescue ritual inside the tiled pool gallery where students once replayed the humiliating clip and later watch the final drill

relational_contract.power_asymmetry: legacy visibility/status power versus scholarship protagonist with no control over her public image
relational_contract.safety_or_kindness_before_power: Eren knows Noa stayed underwater with a panicking child when no camera was recording and trusts that act more than appearance
relational_contract.costly_protagonist_action: she protects a vulnerable person before protecting her appearance or reputation
relational_contract.consent_or_personhood_repair: allies must return authorship and ask consent after trying to arrange her visibility for her
relational_contract.payoff_image: the pool gallery changes from replay-screen humiliation to a safety community where Noa instructs others openly
